answer.note: All four ref files hold the same generic text, so they don't favor any file. I chose by reading the code. The formula is in radon/metrics.py: `mi_compute` combines log(volume), complexity, log(sloc) and sqrt(2.46*radians(comments)), and `mi_rank` handles the bounds. That file should get most of the 60 minutes, about 35. I'd give about 15 to radon/complexity.py, which produces the branch score fed into the formula. About 7 would go to radon/raw.py, which supplies the sloc and comment counts, and about 3 to radon/visitors.py as a skim. I dropped D from the incoming B/D pair because visitors.py doesn't contain the formula. Things to check: the zero and negative guards on log(sloc) and log(volume), the clamp to the 0–100 range, and the comment percentage being converted with radians().
